claims.text: Multi-task learning is a training paradigm in which multiple tasks are simultaneously learned by a shared model.
Deep multi-task learning methods can be partitioned into three main groups: architectures, optimization methods, and task relationship learning.
Inclusion of task-specific channel-wise projection modules decreases the frequency of conflicting gradient update directions across tasks.
Task Routing Layers allow a multi-task network to scale up to 312 tasks simultaneously.
Soft Modularization combined with Soft Actor-Critic achieves a 60% success rate on the MT50 Meta-World benchmark.
PCGrad combined with Soft Actor-Critic successfully completes 70% of tasks on the MT50 Meta-World benchmark.

evidence.description: Multi-task learning (MTL) is a subfield of machine learning in which multiple tasks are simultaneously learned by a shared model.
Our discussion is structured according to a partition of the existing deep MTL techniques into three groups: architectures, optimization methods, and task relationship learning.
it is empirically shown that the inclusion of these task-specific projection modules decreases the chance that gradient update directions for different tasks point in opposite directions
the Task Routing Layer allows for the network to scale up to handle up to 312 tasks simultaneously while maintaining decent performance.
When combined with Soft Actor-Critic (Haarnoja et al., 2018), the Soft Modularization agent reaches 60% success rate on MT50 from the Meta-World benchmark.
When combined with Soft Actor-Critic (Haarnoja et al., 2018), PCGrad is able to successfully complete 70% of the tasks in the MT50 benchmark of the Meta-World environment.

methodologies.name: Taxonomic Literature Review and Survey
methodologies.description: A comprehensive survey categorizing deep multi-task learning into architectures, optimization methods, and task relationship learning.
conditions: Deep neural network multi-task learning literature up to 2020
Fixed task sets learned simultaneously with equal weighting

limitations.text: The survey excludes classical non-neural multi-task learning methods, single main-task auxiliary settings, and settings where the set of tasks changes over time.
Simultaneous learning of multiple tasks can lead to negative transfer or destructive interference when tasks have conflicting requirements.
Conditional computation routing models frequently suffer from module collapse where only a small fraction of available modules are used.

future_work.text: Development of theoretical frameworks and mathematical foundation to understand optimization dynamics and generalization in deep multi-task learning.
